newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BONDS END STEADY, GAP OVER BUNDS WIDENS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BONDS END STEADY, GAP OVER BUNDS WIDENS.

text.p: Bonds ended a quiet session
steady to firmer on Monday overcoming a bearish tone that set
in at the end of last week when the spread to German Bunds
widened beyond the 30 bps of recent weeks, dealers said.
Most of the session's thin trade was in longer maturities,
dealers said.
The downbeat sentiment and the wider spread stemmed from
remarks by a senior Bundesbank official late last week casting
doubt on Finland's participation in the first wave of EMU,
dealers said.
Bonds also reflected weaker Swedish debt, dealers said.
But dealers said the weakness in Sweden was mainly due to
domestic factors, including government spending plans and a plan
to phase out nuclear power, that would not drag on Finnish bonds
for long.
While some dealers said the wider spread to Bunds could
endure in the near term, they said the bearish tone was not
likely to last for long.
The markka was slightly stronger versus the mark, but eased
against the dollar.
DEM/FIM traded in a narrow range, and was seen moving in
2.965 to 2.995 range in the next few days.
--John Acher, Helsinki Newsroom +358-680 50 235
